Overview

About the multi-surface floor & wall vinyl

Textured surface floor graphics grip brick, block paving and rough walls where normal vinyl won't stick. The specialist material is heated into the surface so the print follows every contour, with an R12 anti-slip rating.

  • Anti-slip ratingR12
  • SurfacesBrick, block paving, textured walls
  • PrintFull colour

Every floor graphic is made to measure. Tell us where it's going and how long it needs to last, and we'll recommend the right material and send a proof.

Floor graphics catch attention where people are already looking, which makes them one of the most effective ways to guide visitors and promote products.

Multi-surface vinyl solves a problem every event organiser and retailer has met: normal vinyl simply won't stick to brick, block paving, rough concrete or textured render. This specialist film conforms to the surface when heated, so your graphic follows every contour and grips firmly.

Use it for festival and event wayfinding, pavement promotions outside shops, branded walkways, sports venue graphics and temporary murals on textured walls. The R12 anti-slip finish provides strong grip underfoot.

This film is also used inside, for example on textured warehouse floors, on exposed brick in bars and on concrete in showrooms, where normal floor graphics won't hold. It's a temporary to medium-term solution, ideal for campaigns, events and seasonal routes.

Lifespan depends on footfall, weather and the surface. On a busy pavement in winter it may need replacing sooner than on a sheltered wall. We'll advise on expected lifespan for your location.

Because it bonds into textured surfaces, removal can take longer than with normal floor graphics. On most surfaces it can be peeled away with gentle heat; on very porous surfaces some cleaning may be needed afterwards. We'll advise on removal when you order.

Good design matters on the ground: use large, simple shapes, bold arrows and short words so people can read the graphic while walking.

Installation & fixing

Floors must be clean, dry and free of dust and polish before application. Most floor graphics are designed for short to medium-term use and peel off cleanly when you're done.

Step by step

Application & care guide

  1. 01Prepare the floorClean the floor thoroughly, removing dust, polish and grease, and let it dry completely.
  2. 02PositionLay the graphic in place and mark its position with masking tape.
  3. 03ApplyPeel back part of the liner, smooth the graphic down from one edge, and press firmly, especially at the edges.
  4. 04Check gripMake sure all edges are sealed so they can't catch feet or cleaning equipment.
  5. 05Care and removalSweep and damp-mop; avoid scrubbing machines. Peel off slowly when the campaign ends.
Artwork

Artwork guide

Getting your artwork right first time means a sharper sign and a faster turnaround. No file? Our studio can help.

  • Best file types: vector files (AI, EPS, SVG or a PDF exported from design software) give razor-sharp results at any size. High-resolution JPG, PNG or TIFF files work for photos.
  • Resolution: for photos and raster images, aim for at least 150dpi at the final printed size (300dpi for small signs viewed close up). Images taken from websites or social media are usually too small.
  • Colours: set artwork up in CMYK. If your brand has Pantone or RAL references, tell us and we'll match them as closely as the material allows.
  • Fonts: convert text to outlines or embed fonts in your PDF, so the lettering prints exactly as designed.
  • Bleed and margins: add 3 to 5mm bleed around printed panels and keep important text at least 10mm from the edge.
  • Cut-to-shape signs: include the cut line as a separate vector path. If you don't have one, our studio will create it.
  • No artwork? Send us your logo, wording and any brand guidelines and our design studio will lay it out for you. You'll see a proof before anything is made.
Questions

Multi-Surface Floor & Wall Vinyl FAQs

Can't see your question? Call 01603 407786 or send an enquiry.

Are floor graphics slippery?

Our vinyl floor graphics have anti-slip laminates rated R11 or R12.

How long do they last?

It depends on foot traffic; expect several months in busy areas.

Do they leave residue?

Most peel off cleanly from sealed floors.

Do I need a fitter?

Yes, it's heat-applied and best fitted by experienced installers.

Can it go on tarmac?

Ask us; surface condition affects performance.

How long does it last?

It depends on footfall, weather and the surface; we'll advise for your location.

Is it removable?

Yes, it can be removed, though very rough surfaces may need extra care.

How is it removed?

Usually by peeling with gentle heat; porous surfaces may need cleaning afterwards.

Is it safe for people walking on it?

Yes, the R12 anti-slip finish gives strong grip underfoot, including in wet conditions, which is why it's used at events and on busy pavements.
